case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment heading: Suresh Singhal v. State (Delhi Administration).

number_of_accused.reason: Only the appellant's liability is decided; the father died during pendency and the third accused was acquitted.

accused_gender.quote: The appellant reached for his revolver
accused_gender.reason: Accused is male; the judgment uses 'he' and 'his' for the appellant and refers to his son and father.

accused_age.reason: No age of the appellant is stated anywhere in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is described.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: The judgment does not state the appellant's occupation; the property dealer is the deceased.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class; 'licensed revolvers' alone does not state status.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: The deceased-Shyam Sunder and Kishan Lal, both brothers, were killed
victim_gender.reason: Both victims who died were male brothers.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victims is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victims is described.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: a dispute that had arisen between the appellant and the deceased
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Dispute over property sale through the deceased as property dealer is described by the judgment.

offence_category.quote: the homicide falls within Exception 4 to Section 300 of IPC and does not amount to murder
offence_category.reason: Charged as murder, but the finally established offence is culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC s.302 and s.304 read with s.34; s.307 read with s.34 (attempt to murder Hans Raj, referred to as a conviction); IPC s.97 and s.300 Exceptions 2 and 4 discussed
statutory_provisions.quote: Sessions Court convicted the appellant for the murder of Shyam Sunder under Sections 302 and 304 read with Section 34
statutory_provisions.reason: Omits the s.307 attempt conviction referred to at para 37 and the s.97 and s.300 Exception provisions applied.

weapon.quote: It is thus not possible to determine the weapon that was used by the appellant-Suresh Singhal.
weapon.reason: Appellant's .32 Smith & Wesson revolver was recovered, but ballistics could not determine the weapon used.

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical, ballistic and recovery evidence are all discussed in the judgment.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating facts are noted by the court; the prosecution's undue advantage argument was rejected.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: the exercise of the right was in good faith, in his own defence and without premeditation
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Sudden fight, private defence, no premeditation and no undue advantage are all supported by the judgment.

trial_court_outcome.quote: The Sessions Court convicted the appellant for the murder of Shyam Sunder under Sections 302 and 304
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction under ss.302 and 304 r/w s.34 is stated; trial sentence is not given in the judgment.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: High Court judgment dated 01.09.2010 (Crl. A. 232/1997) on appellant's appeal; State's appeal (Crl. A. 226/1997) against acquittal of Roshan Lal dismissed; appellant's convictions were under challenge before the Supreme Court
high_court_outcome.quote: The appeal filed by the State seeking death penalty for the appellant and against the acquittal of Roshal Lal was dismissed by the High Court
high_court_outcome.reason: State's appeal was against Roshan Lal's acquittal; the appellant's own High Court outcome is not expressly stated.

final_outcome.quote: his conviction under section 304 IPC is maintained
final_outcome.reason: Conviction altered from s.302 to s.304 for the deaths, so conviction_modified is correct.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: IPC s.304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) for the deaths of Shyam Sunder and Kishan Lal
offence_finally_established.quote: his conviction under section 304 IPC is maintained
offence_finally_established.reason: Omits that the s.304 conviction also stands for Kishan Lal's death after the s.302 conviction was set aside.

imprisonment_type.quote: we sentence him under section 304 IPC to the period already undergone
imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is a term equal to the period already undergone, a fixed-term sentence in effect.

imprisonment_years.quote: sentence of 13 Y:z years as on date
imprisonment_years.reason: Sentence equals about 13.5 years already undergone as on the date of judgment.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is imposed or mentioned.

neutral_facts.correct_value: A neutral summary of the prosecution and defence accounts and the physical and ballistic evidence, without the Court's reconstruction of the sequence (para 15) as witness evidence
neutral_facts.quote: The appellant reached for his revolver, upon which the deceased released him and turned around to run away.
neutral_facts.reason: The release-and-turn sequence is the Court's own reconstruction (para 15), not trial testimony, and leans toward the Court's reasoning.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment does not state the statutory punishment for s.302 or s.304.

attempt_completion.reason: Both victims were killed, so the offence was completed as to the deaths.

physical_harm.quote: Three .32 bullets were recovered from the body of deceased Kishan Lal.
physical_harm.reason: Two deaths by gunshot and a surviving brother hit by bullets are all supported.

number_of_offences.correct_value: 3 charged (IPC ss.302, 304 and 307, each r/w s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.304)
number_of_offences.quote: his conviction for attempt to murder Hans Raj for which he has been convicted
number_of_offences.reason: Omits the s.307 attempt-to-murder charge/conviction the appellant faced for Hans Raj.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is discussed; property sale was the dispute only.

premeditation_planning.quote: the homicide was not the result of premeditation but rather ... the shooting took place in a sudden fight in the heat of passion
premeditation_planning.reason: Court found no premeditation, relying on the Sessions and High Court findings.

motive.quote: a dispute that had arisen between the appellant and the deceased
motive.reason: Property sale dispute is marked as alleged, which is acceptable as the court did not decide the motive.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: PW-23 and PW-27 on scuffle, medical distant-range evidence, trajectory and ballistic report are all relied on by the Court.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-3 and PW-30 rejected on the no-scuffle version (PW-30 inconsistent with wound position); PW-27 unshaken and accepted; PW-23 accepted on scuffle; PW-3 did not specify that the appellant shot Kishan Lal
witness_credibility.quote: Yet this witness does not specify that the appellant shot him.
witness_credibility.reason: Court did not find PW-3 not credible on who fired; it found his evidence did not specify the appellant as shooter.

post_offence_conduct.quote: the appellant and his father ... fled the place in the car of another visitor
post_offence_conduct.reason: Flight from the scene is noted in the judgment's incident narrative; it is labelled as prosecution account, which is accurate.

custody_duration.reason: Approximately 13.5 years undergone as on date of judgment and the appellant is in jail.

bail_history.reason: No bail history is mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date 04.03.1991, High Court 01.09.2010, Supreme Court 02.02.2017 are given; trial judgment date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: Sushil Kumar, S. K. Aggarwal, Sr. Advs. ... for the Appellant. P. K. Dey ... for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Appellant and State counsel names match the judgment's listing.

investigation_status.reason: The judgment does not state FIR, charge sheet or investigation completion details.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the Court.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 304 r/w s.34. High Court: judgment dated 01.09.2010 under challenge (Crl. A. 232/1997). Supreme Court: s.302 convictions for Shyam Sunder and Kishan Lal altered to s.304; sentence of period already undergone
appeal_history.quote: we are of the view that Suresh Singhal is undoubtedly guilty of causing death to Shyam Sunder ... under Section 304
appeal_history.reason: Omits that the s.302 conviction for Shyam Sunder was also altered to s.304 by the Supreme Court.

prosecution_argument.quote: the appellant took undue advantage of the situation and used the gun even though the deceased and his brothers were unarmed
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution argued the deceased were unarmed and the appellant took undue advantage by using the gun.

defence_argument.quote: the deceased tried to strangulate the appellant ... It is not possible for us to accept the argument that ... Pritpal Singhal ... fired the shot
defence_argument.reason: Private defence during strangulation and the alternative father-fired argument were both advanced by counsel.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Private defence under s.97 with Darshan Singh principles and Exceptions 2 and 4 to s.300 were applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Darshan Singh v. State of Punjab and Another (2010) 2 SCC 333
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Darshan Singh is the only precedent relied on, with citation matching the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.quote: we sentence him under section 304 IPC to the period already undergone
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale is the Exception 4 finding and s.304 guilt; the Court gave no further sentencing reasons.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: the exercise of the right was in good faith, in his own defence and without premeditation
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Good faith, no premeditation, sudden fight and no undue advantage were weighed by the Court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court weighed no aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.quote: He be released forthwith from the custody, if not required in any other case.
other_sentence_order.reason: Direction for release forthwith if not required in any other case is stated.
